chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who returns from his journey and the time for prayer has entered. He said: 'He should pray two rak'at. And when he goes out on a journey and the time for prayer has entered, let him pray four (rak'at).'
ai.seo_question: When should a traveler shorten their prayer versus praying fully according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the critical distinction between the state of being a traveler (musafir) and a resident (muqim) at the precise moment the prayer time enters. It establishes that if one is already in the state of travel when the time begins, the prayer is shortened (qasr); conversely, if the prayer time enters while one is still at home, the prayer is performed in full (tamam) even if one departs immediately after. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly principle that the status of the prayer is determined by the condition of the worshipper at the onset of the prayer time.
